text:
alex: Heads-up — on canary cluster I'm seeing steady memory growth for long chat sessions (>=18k tokens). Root trace points to page reuse with shifted token offsets, looks like a prefix alignment drift that accumulates across requests.

maria: Can you paste the smallest repro + logs? Is this only on the canary kernel or everywhere?

alex: Repro (run for ~2000 steps to see growth):
```bash
REDWOOD_ENV=canary ./bin/serve --model redwood-13b --max-context 20000 --batch-size 1 \\n  --kv-cache-mode=prefix

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat -d '{"input": "repeat long paragraph..."}'
```
Log extract (snippet):
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] kv_page_fetch id=0x7f9 start=4096 len=4096 tag=32 token_offset=0
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] kv_page_append id=0x7f9 start=8192 len=4096 tag=33 token_offset=15  <-- offset != expected
[2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] evict_page id=0x7f9 tombstone=0x0 
[2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] kv_page_fetch id=0x7f9 start=4096 len=4096 tag=32 token_offset=15  <-- stale offset reused
```
This ends up producing token alignment mismatch and then stale embeddings for that region.

cheng: Interesting. I sampled a perf profile while reproducing — top stacks show heavy time in `align_kv_tags` and `copy_prefix_pages`. Also `select_kernel_for_seq` spikes when sequence > 1024. My hunch: kernel selection path does a fast-path memcpy assuming page-aligned tokens for some quantized kernels; when batching heuristics trigger a different kernel the expected alignment shifts and we end up writing an offset into an already-live page.

maria: So the bug is not the eviction itself but that an append writes with a wrong offset and we don't zero or update the expected tag?

alex: Exactly. I tried forcing a full page zero before append and the mem growth stops, but that's expensive. Patch idea: write a small sentinel at the page boundary when we flush, and assert on read. Would catch but not prevent.

jonathan: Two vectors: short-term mitigation (cheap) + root fix. Short-term: enforce `flush_on_context_switch` when kernel selection changes (i.e., if new kernel != current kernel, evict/flush affected pages). That should prevent cross-request contamination at cost of some perf for mixed-kernel workloads. Root fix: fix the offset computation in `batch_append()` so writes respect the page's `base_token_offset` regardless of kernel path.

cheng: I reproduced with a unit test that does repeated alternating small and large batches (to flip kernel choice). Test fails with the old code after ~300 iterations. I can push the failing test. It asserts `page.base_token_offset == expected_offset` but sees `expected + 15`.

alex: Pushed log and repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/xxxx (link). Also saw this on dedicated dev pool under heavy interleaving (different tenant requests). That means cross-request contamination risk for Dedicated customers — we should treat this as P1 for canary -> release branch.

maria: Agreed. Please add the failing test and a short perf benchmark so we can evaluate mitigation cost. Also tag infra for a quick canary rollback plan if the hotfix regresses latency. @infra-bot can you create a canary incident ticket?

infra-bot: New ticket created: CANARY-3482 "prefix alignment bleed: repro & hotfix" — assigned to eng-runtime, priority=P1.

jonathan: My quick patch (WIP): in `batch_append()` normalize `write_offset = (page.base_token_offset + local_offset) % PAGE_TOKENS` and assert `write_offset < PAGE_TOKENS`. Also add a defensive `memset(page.addr + write_offset, 0, pad)` for the tail if `local_offset` would overlap. This should remove stale-token reads.

cheng: That sounds good. Adding the unit test + benchmark. One ask: include a feature-flag to enable stricter flushing so ops can rollback without code changes.

alex: Ran jonathan's WIP on canary with feature-flag=false (i.e., only offset normalization + tail zeroing). No memory growth after 100k iterations, throughput drop ~1.7% on microbench for 8k seqs. With flush mitigation enabled throughput drops ~8% but stabilizes memory.

maria: OK plan: patch + CI test in PR; run perf gates (baseline + mitigation); backport to release with feature-flag default off. We'll enable flag on a small % of canary hosts and monitor. If stable, flip on by default then release.

jonathan: I'll open PR: GH-#4128. Put the unit test under `eng-runtime/tests/kv_align_regress.cc` and add a short perf runner.

cheng: Also adding a tracing tracepoint to log `kernel_id` and `page_token_offset` on append so we can correlate in prod without verbose logs.

alex: Thanks all. Leaving the repro running overnight — if anyone wants access to canary logs ping me. :eyes: :bug:

maria: Good work. After PR lands, let's add a postmortem checklist so we catch mixed-kernel alignment in future kernels.

jonathan: Will do.
